title: NeetCode 250 master problem pattern audit

scope.basis: Exclude named page sections, not every occurrence of those concepts elsewhere. This preserves the previously agreed 180 problems.

method: Classified every included primary JavaScript solution and every displayed JavaScript follow-up from the resolved solutionMap; inspected Python for noted implementation differences. Each version has a source hash and a required invariant or variation. This is a curriculum coverage audit, not a fresh judge run or a catalog of every possible alternative algorithm.
countMeaning: Study-unit boundaries are editorial. The count includes specialized techniques and variants; it is not a canonical or minimal number of algorithms.
coverageMeaning: All included entries and displayed JavaScript versions are mapped. No master lesson is implemented or validated by this audit. A lesson must demonstrate each mapped variation before it may be called covered.

acceptanceCriteria: Every included problem and displayed alternative maps to at least one implemented study unit and its required variation.
A category label, shared data structure, or common loop shape alone never counts as coverage.
Each lesson supplies explicit input constraints, expected output, state, invariant, full JavaScript code, and a reason each update is valid.
Each mapped variation has an example that exercises it, including adversarial cases where a superficially similar template fails.
Walkthrough events come from executing the displayed code; highlight ranges and data changes match that version. No artificial noop steps or premature structures.
Show expanded complexity costs and their simplification; preserve the agreed O(1) FIFO convention and distinguish heap costs and output construction.
Keep all excluded-section overlaps visible; excluding those concepts everywhere would change the 180-problem scope.
Recheck source hashes and the page inventory before claiming the audit is current.
